title.narrative: Climate change and refugee health in the MENA region: co-producing a research agenda

description.narrative: Aim: This Global Health Development project aims to establish new partnerships between the American University of Beirut, Imperial College London, and other Middle East and North Africa (MENA) regional partners on a research agenda about climate change and refugee health. In this project, we aim to develop a conceptual framework and define and refine research questions, based on existing knowledge and the needs of the community and relevant actors. We will then use these outputs to produce a future research programme on climate change and refugee health with our partners. Project workplan: We will identify and establish fair and long-lasting partnerships to conduct the project and produce a future research proposal. Our project workplan includes: (i) Exploratory research to identify gaps in the research literature and policy guidelines on refugee health and climate change in Lebanon and the MENA region. Using this information, we will draft a conceptual framework to understand how climate change affects refugee health. (ii) We will invite relevant actors, including decision-makers and humanitarian sector representatives, to join a Stakeholder Advisory Group to understand their key priorities and needs through interactive workshops. (iii) We will identify the needs and priorities of refugees through Refugee Community Group workshops and regular meetings. Moreover, in further workshops with the refugee community and relevant actors, we will seek input to improve the conceptual framework and refine the important research questions. (iv) We will train and strengthen the partners and team on writing research proposals and identified needs.
